overview: Data#3 is a Brisbane-headquartered, ASX-listed IT services and solutions provider operating across Australia and the Pacific Islands (Fiji), with roots dating to 1979 and ASX-listed since 1997. It resells and integrates hardware, software and cloud subscriptions from major vendors (Microsoft, Cisco, HP/HPE, Dell, Adobe, Palo Alto, Veeam) and wraps them with its own Services business (consulting, project, managed and maintenance services) for a base of 5,000+ mostly government, education, health and large-corporate customers. The company reports 'Total Gross Sales' (~$3.4bn in FY2026) as its primary operating KPI because statutory revenue is recognised on a net/agency basis for software licensing and vendor-delivered maintenance, making reported IFRS revenue (~$907m FY2026) a small fraction of the sales volume actually transacted.

business_model.summary: Data#3 earns its margin as a reseller/agent and services integrator, not as a manufacturer: it takes principal (gross) revenue recognition on hardware and internally-delivered services, but agent (net) recognition on third-party software licensing and vendor-delivered maintenance (an FY2024 accounting policy change). Consequently overall gross margin on Total Gross Sales is structurally thin (9.0% in FY26, down from 9.6% in FY25) while gross margin on statutory net revenue is much higher (~34%+ in Services, ~13% in Infrastructure). Profitability is driven by services attach, vendor rebates/incentives, deal-margin management and tight internal cost control (Internal Cost Ratio, i.e. staff + operating expenses as % of gross profit, which improved to 77.5% in FY26 from 79.7% in FY25) rather than by volume alone. The business also earns meaningful interest income (~$10.1m in FY26) on a large customer-funded cash float, since Data#3 collects from customers and pays vendors on different terms.

revenue_streams.name: Software Solutions (licensing, cloud/CSP subscriptions, Azure, security software)
Infrastructure Solutions (end-user compute, data centre, networking, devices)
Services (consulting, project, managed, maintenance, People Solutions recruitment)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2G — federal, state and local government, education, health and resources sectors plus large corporates; SME expansion underway
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia (all states/territories, 8 regions) plus Fiji/Pacific Islands; predominantly domestic, no meaningful FX revenue exposure from operations

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest independent ASX-listed IT services/reseller-integrators in Australia; long-standing #1 or top-tier partner status with Microsoft, Cisco and HP across ANZ/APJC, giving it scale advantages in a fragmented, highly competitive reseller/integrator market (management itself describes the NSW market as 'highly competitive and disaggregated')

moat_factors.description: 45+ years of accumulated vendor certifications and advisory-board relationships with Microsoft, Cisco, HP, HPE, Dell, Palo Alto, Adobe, Veeam create switching costs for vendors and differentiate technical depth versus smaller resellers, but the moat is rentable rather than owned — vendor program changes (e.g., Microsoft's Dec-2024 incentive restructure, Cisco's 360 Partner Program rebate reshuffle) can unilaterally compress economics

In March 2026 the Digital Transformation Agency appointed Data#3 as the sole panel provider of Microsoft products and services to the Australian Government under a new five-year Volume Sourcing Arrangement (with a further one-year extension option) — the largest contract in Data#3's history, extending a role it has held continuously since the VSA's 2008 inception. Data#3 was also reappointed to the renewed NSW Government Microsoft software panel in FY26, supporting the majority of NSW agencies' Microsoft Enterprise Agreement renewals. These long-run panel incumbencies create high re-tender switching costs and multi-year revenue visibility that smaller competitors cannot easily contest

Large, debt-free balance sheet ($326.0m cash at 30 June 2026, down from $356.7m a year earlier; net assets $95.2m) allows Data#3 to fund large enterprise agreements and earn float interest income that smaller competitors cannot replicate
High customer satisfaction scores (4.36/5 in FY26), HRD Employer of Choice for eleven consecutive years, and Great Place to Work accreditation support retention of both staff and customers
Recurring gross sales (multi-year EA/CSP subscriptions, DaaS, managed services, HPE GreenLake) rose to 70% of gross sales in FY26 (from 69% in FY25), improving revenue visibility

weaknesses: Structurally thin gross margin on gross sales (9.0% in FY26, down from 9.6% in FY25) leaves little room for cost or incentive shocks to flow straight through to the bottom line

Heavy dependence on a small number of global vendors (especially Microsoft, which represents a large share of Software Solutions) for channel economics it does not control — Software Solutions average gross margin fell from 3.6% to 3.4% in FY26 on the Microsoft EA incentive reset
Reseller/integrator model has limited differentiation and low barriers to entry at the transactional (non-services) end, exposing Data#3 to price competition on large enterprise deals
Public sector customer concentration creates cyclicality around state/federal election cycles and government budget/contracting policy

People Solutions recruitment arm exposed to broader Australian labour market softness (gross sales down 8.7% in FY26) and Project Services also weakened (down 15.3%), unrelated to core IT resale economics

growth_drivers: AI-driven IT spend: Gartner forecasts ~8.9% growth in Australian IT spending for 2026, with Software (+13.6%) and Data Centre (+22.5%) segments outgrowing the market as enterprises invest in GenAI/agentic AI and supporting infrastructure

Windows 11 / device refresh supercycle driving End User Compute growth (Infrastructure Solutions gross sales +14.1% in FY26) as customers migrate ahead of Windows 10 end-of-support, plus emerging AI-capable PC demand

Shift to recurring/annuity revenue — multi-year Enterprise Agreements, Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) subscriptions, Device-as-a-Service (>100% growth in FY26) and HPE GreenLake — now 70% of gross sales, improving earnings quality

DTA five-year sole-panel Microsoft Volume Sourcing Arrangement (announced March 2026, largest contract in company history) and renewed NSW Government Microsoft software panel provide a multi-year public-sector revenue platform

Managed Services expansion (gross sales +9.4% FY26), new Managed Extended Detection & Response and a new 24x7 Sovereign Security Operations Centre launching in FY27 to address data-sovereignty/regulated-industry cyber demand

Data#3's own AI practice (dedicated FY27 AI Practice and customer-facing AI delivery pods) plus internal AI adoption (automation across procurement, software development, cyber security and customer experience workflows) lifting operating efficiency/ICR

Public sector recovery after FY25's federal and Queensland state election-related decision-making delays; Brisbane 2032 Olympics infrastructure seen as a multi-year opportunity given Data#3's Brisbane HQ and stadium/venue project experience

Continued margin recovery in Infrastructure Solutions and Services as automation, restructuring benefits and mix shift toward higher-margin managed/security offerings continue to lower the Internal Cost Ratio (improved to 77.5% in FY26 from 79.7% in FY25)

business.description: Microsoft's Dec-2024 restructure of Enterprise Agreement incentives compressed Software Solutions gross margin from 3.6% to 3.4% in FY26; a further FY27 overhaul removes 'Core' CSP incentives for Microsoft 365/Dynamics 365 indirect resellers and applies a 5% margin cut on some legacy products from October 2026 — an ongoing structural risk given Microsoft's outsized share of Software Solutions. Separately, Cisco's 360 Partner Program changes have already begun shifting rebates from Maintenance Services (Services segment) to Infrastructure Solutions, which Data#3 has so far offset by winning preferred-partner status across Networking, Collaboration, Cloud/AI, Security and Services specialisations

Reliance on a handful of large global technology vendors for product and margin, and on large government/enterprise accounts (including the new DTA five-year sole-panel Microsoft VSA) for a meaningful share of gross sales
9.0% blended gross margin on Total Gross Sales in FY26 (down from 9.6% in FY25) means small percentage-point shifts in mix or vendor terms have outsized effects on profit
Growth in Services and Managed Services strategic focus areas depends on continued ability to attract/retain scarce technical talent

FY26 was a mixed year for Services: Business Aspect consulting (+22%) and Maintenance Services (+11.5%) grew strongly, but Project Services gross sales fell 15.3% (reduced business confidence, extended procurement, softer conversion in QLD/VIC/WA) and People Solutions fell 8.7% (soft labour market); management describes FY26 as 'the start of a multi-year transition for Project Services' with a new leadership team and strategy only commencing execution in FY27

financial.description: Operating cash flow is highly seasonal (heavy EOFY invoicing/collection in June creates large swings between reporting periods); FY26 net operating cash inflow fell to $23.3m from $126.3m in FY25 due to timing of customer receipts around the June/July peak, and closing inventory rose sharply to $73.4m (from $18.4m) as the company pre-bought hardware ahead of expected price rises from the global memory-chip shortage

A meaningful profit contributor (~$10.1m in FY26, down slightly from $10.2m in FY25) comes from interest earned on cash float; falling interest rates in Australia would be a modest earnings headwind even as they support customer IT spending sentiment

regulatory.description: Government policy on contractor use versus direct employment, and machinery-of-government changes after elections, can delay or reshape public sector spending, though the new DTA sole-panel VSA and NSW panel renewal lock in Data#3's position through the medium term

Growing government requirements for data sovereignty (driving Data#3's new 24x7 Sovereign SOC, layered on its existing hybrid Brisbane-based SOC) require ongoing compliance investment but also create a growth opportunity if executed well

macro.description: High inflation/interest rates historically slowed customer IT procurement decisions; the FY26 annual report notes inflationary and interest-rate pressures showed signs of easing during the year but customers continued to exercise caution, with some procurement, approval and contracting decisions taking longer to complete
State and federal election cycles (Queensland, federal) have repeatedly caused temporary delays to public-sector decision-making and sales, as seen in FY25 and flagged as an ongoing mitigated risk

A global memory-chip shortage during FY26 drove higher hardware prices and reduced availability for PCs, network equipment and servers; Data#3 mitigated the impact through warehousing and vendor relationships (and pre-buying inventory), but the FY26 letter to shareholders flags these conditions are expected to persist through the remainder of calendar 2026

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian IT spending is forecast by Gartner to grow ~8.9% in CY2026 (to over A$172bn), with Software (+13.6%), Data Centre (+22.5%) and Devices (+6.6%) all growing, driven substantially by GenAI/agentic AI adoption, cybersecurity investment and Windows 11/device refresh cycles
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — IT discretionary spend (project services, device refresh, consulting) is sensitive to interest rates, business/consumer confidence and government election cycles, but a growing recurring/annuity revenue base (70% of gross sales) and a large public-sector customer base (anchored by the new 5-year DTA sole-panel Microsoft VSA) provide some counter-cyclical stability versus pure commercial IT resellers
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate: falling rates are a net positive via improved customer IT investment sentiment, offsetting a modest reduction in the company's own float/interest income (~$10m/yr on large cash balances)
key_input_costs: Vendor-set hardware/software wholesale pricing and rebate structures (particularly Microsoft and Cisco)

Device/component costs subject to global semiconductor and memory supply and pricing — a global memory-chip shortage drove higher hardware prices through FY26 and is expected to persist into late CY2026

recent_developments.event: Microsoft announced changes to partner incentive programs effective 1 January 2025 (reducing Enterprise Agreement incentives, shifting focus/incentives to CSP, Copilot, Security and Azure migrations); DTL shares fell sharply (~13%) on the initial announcement, foreshadowing a subsequent margin squeeze

1H FY26 results showed record gross sales (+9.2% to $1.54bn) but Software gross margin compressed from ~4.0% to ~3.5% on the Microsoft incentive changes; shares fell ~6-14% on the result as the market questioned whether the ~26x P/E could be sustained against only ~3.6% first-half earnings growth

Data#3 announced its appointment by the Digital Transformation Agency (DTA) as the sole panel provider of Microsoft products and services to the Australian Government, under a new five-year Volume Sourcing Arrangement (with a further one-year extension option) — the largest contract in the Company's history, extending a role it has held continuously since the VSA's inception in 2008. Data#3 was also reappointed to the renewed NSW Government Microsoft software panel

FY2026 full-year results (year ended 30 June 2026) confirmed by the full statutory Annual Report (filed 2026-09-17): statutory revenue up 6.4% to $907.3m, total gross profit up 5.3% to $305.2m (margin 9.0%, down from 9.6%), EBIT up 16.6% to $69.8m, NPBT up 14.0% to $78.8m, NPAT up 13.1% to $54.5m, EPS up 13.0% to 35.16 cents, Internal Cost Ratio improved to 77.5% (from 79.7%), and fully franked full-year dividends up 13.0% to 31.75 cents (90.3% payout ratio). Total Gross Sales rose 12.7% to a record $3.385bn. Cash fell to $326.0m (from $356.7m) and net operating cash inflow fell to $23.3m (from $126.3m) on EOFY receipt timing; inventory rose to $73.4m (from $18.4m) as the Company pre-bought hardware ahead of memory-chip-shortage price rises

Growth by solution area/segment in FY26 (gross sales): Infrastructure Solutions +14.1%, Software Solutions +14.1%, Services +3.6% (Business Aspect consulting +22%, Maintenance Services +11.5%, Managed Services +9.4%, offset by Project Services -15.3% and People Solutions -8.7%); Device-as-a-Service grew >100%

FY2026 statutory Annual Report (filed 17 September 2026, five days before this review) confirmed no formal quantitative FY27 revenue/EPS guidance was given, consistent with long-standing practice; management reiterated qualitative FY27 priorities (dedicated AI Practice and customer-facing AI delivery pods, 24x7 Sovereign Security Operations Centre, more disciplined Services sales/segmentation strategy, Microsoft AI Frontier Accelerate programs) and flagged the FY27 Microsoft CSP 'Core' incentive removal (effective October 2026) as a continuing but manageable headwind via fee-based revenue substitution. Financial Calendar confirms: final dividend record date 16 September 2026, payment date 30 September 2026, AGM 28 October 2026, H1 FY27 results 22 February 2027

The Annual Report noted with sadness the recent unexpected passing of Richard Anderson OAM, Data#3's founding-era Non-Executive Director and Chair for 23 of his 26 years on the Board (retired late 2023), a governance/legacy note rather than a current operational matter

Board renewal: Susan Forrester and Leanne Muller retired as Non-Executive Directors; Bronwyn Morris AM appointed Dec-2024, Diana Eilert and Laurence Baynham (former long-serving CEO/MD, 1994-2024) appointed as Non-Executive Directors effective 1 July 2025

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Report (filed 17 September 2026) / FY2026 Results Announcement (24 August 2026)

items.notes: Consistent with long-standing practice, Data#3 does not provide specific quantitative FY guidance in its results announcement or Annual Report; management instead frames qualitative growth priorities (Solutions, Customer Experience, Operational Excellence, People and Community) and directional commentary. The Annual Report's Strategy and Outlook section reiterates the Company 'enters FY27 with a clear strategy...and sustained earnings growth for shareholders' without a numeric target

items.metric: Internal Cost Ratio (staff + opex / gross profit)
items.notes: Management guided ICR to hold near FY2026 levels despite continued investment in the new AI Practice and Sovereign SOC

After FY26 growth of 7.6% depressed by the Microsoft incentive reset, management expects normalization as the reset annualises, Microsoft's AI Frontier Accelerate program ramps, and fee-based/advisory revenue substitutes for lost rebates

FY27 Services plan targets a more integrated practice model, stronger sales discipline and clearer ownership of offerings across Consulting, Project Services, Managed Services and resourcing, with priority capability in Data and AI, cyber security/sovereignty, Microsoft services, Managed Azure and Unified Endpoint Management, after a mixed FY26 (Project Services -15.3%, People Solutions -8.7%)
Reflects continued investment in the new AI Practice, Sovereign SOC and services delivery headcount, even as FY26 internal staff costs grew a modest 2%

items.metric: Net profit investment drag (AI Practice + Sovereign SOC)
items.notes: One-off/step-up investment cost called out separately by management for the two new FY27 capability build-outs
Assumes broadly stable cash interest rates through most of FY2027 on the company's large customer-funded cash float ($326.0m at 30 June 2026)

items.target: Manageable, largely offset by fee-based revenue substitution
items.notes: Removal of 'Core' CSP incentives for Microsoft 365/Dynamics 365 indirect resellers and a 5% margin cut on some legacy/standalone products from October 2026; management says it is replacing lost rebate profit with direct advisory/subscription-optimisation fees, building on the strategy that let Software Solutions gross profit exceed expectations (a 'flat year-on-year' internal target) in FY26

items.target: Continue high, fully franked payout ratio (FY26: 90.3%)
items.notes: Board endorsed a new capital management framework in FY26 designed to preserve financial resilience, fund organic growth and strategic investment, and deliver consistent shareholder returns; final FY26 dividend of 31.75 cents record date 16 September 2026, paid 30 September 2026; AGM scheduled 28 October 2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Brad Colledge said FY26's performance 'reinforces our agility and the continued strength of our people, strategy and business model,' and in the Annual Report stated Data#3 'enter[s] FY27 with a clear strategy, strong vendor partnerships, a broad and loyal customer base, a strong balance sheet and a growing portfolio of solutions across AI, cyber security, cloud, data, infrastructure and managed services.' Chair Mark Gray highlighted the Board's new capital management framework and 14% growth in earnings before tax to $78.8 million. CFO commentary (from the FY26 results call) indicated flat operating leverage (ICR) is the base case for FY27 despite continued growth investment, and that the FY27 Microsoft CSP changes are expected to be manageable given the fee-substitution strategy already proven through FY26.

bull_case: Long, consistent compounding track record: NPAT grown from ~$23.6m (FY20) to $54.5m (FY26), EPS up from 15.35 cents to 35.16 cents, and dividends up from 13.90 to 31.75 cents, funded almost entirely from organic operations with no bank debt; FY26 total shareholder return of 333% (including dividends) on a 30 June 2026 share price of $9.85
Debt-free balance sheet with a large cash float ($326.0m at June 2026) earning meaningful interest income (~$10-11m/yr), providing resilience and optionality without shareholder dilution risk

New DTA five-year sole-panel Microsoft VSA for the Australian Government (announced March 2026, the largest contract in Data#3's history) and renewed NSW Microsoft panel entrench public-sector incumbency and improve multi-year revenue visibility just as Microsoft simultaneously reduces channel economics

Structural AI/cloud/security tailwinds (Gartner forecasts ~8.9% Australian IT spend growth in 2026) directly benefit Data#3's core Software, Infrastructure and Services lines, with a dedicated FY27 AI Practice and Sovereign SOC building on FY26's AI-related sales growth

Rising recurring/annuity revenue mix (70% of gross sales) from multi-year Enterprise Agreements, CSP subscriptions, DaaS (>100% growth) and managed services improves earnings visibility and quality over time

Management has demonstrated it can offset vendor incentive shocks (the FY26 Microsoft reset, Cisco's 360 Partner Program changes) through cost discipline (ICR improved to 77.5% from 79.7%) and fee-based revenue substitution, delivering accelerating full-year profit growth (EBIT +16.6%, NPAT +13.1%) despite a rocky H1 FY26
bear_case: High dependence on Microsoft's channel economics, which the vendor can and does unilaterally change (the FY26 EA incentive cuts that compressed Software Solutions margin from 3.6% to 3.4%, and a further FY27 CSP 'Core' incentive removal plus legacy-product margin cuts from October 2026), creating recurring earnings-quality risk in the largest segment (Software Solutions, ~68% of gross sales) even as the new DTA panel deepens that dependence

Structurally thin and declining gross margin (9.0% of Total Gross Sales in FY26, down from 9.6% in FY25) leaves little buffer to absorb vendor, competitive or cost shocks; the H1 FY26 sell-off (shares down ~6-14%) showed how quickly the market re-rates the stock on margin disappointment even with strong top-line growth

Services segment (13% of gross sales) is not firing uniformly: Project Services (-15.3%) and People Solutions (-8.7%) both declined in FY26 on softer business confidence, extended procurement cycles and a weak labour market, and management itself frames FY27 as only 'the start' of a Project Services turnaround

No meaningful moat beyond vendor certifications, government panel incumbency and scale — it remains fundamentally a reseller/integrator business in a 'highly competitive and disaggregated' Australian IT services market with numerous domestic and global competitors (DXC, NTT, CSG, Interactive, Insight, Computacenter, Datacom)

Valuation has historically run at a premium multiple (~26x P/E cited around the H1 FY26 sell-off); sell-side consensus price targets (roughly A$8.4-8.95 average across ~10 analysts as of September 2026) sit meaningfully below the A$9.85 30 June 2026 close, implying the market or the Street is pricing limited further upside without continued double-digit earnings growth through the FY27 Microsoft CSP transition
